heroIntro: The right base, the right rate, the right filing: Zakat and income tax computed correctly for Saudi and GCC-owned shares and for foreign-owned shares.
overview: Saudi entities with mixed ownership have to split their results between Zakat and income tax. Getting the ownership allocation and the Zakat base right matters, because errors surface at assessment. We compute both, prepare the annual declaration and the supporting financial statements, and support assessments with reconciliations and draft explanations.

Prepare the annual declaration and supporting financial statements.
Compute withholding tax on payments to non-residents and prepare returns.
Support assessments with reconciliations and draft explanations.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Zakat and income tax in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.a: Zakat generally applies to Saudi and GCC-owned shares, while income tax applies to foreign-owned shares. Entities with mixed ownership compute both on their respective portions.

faqs.q: Do you handle withholding tax on payments abroad?
faqs.a: Yes. We compute withholding tax on payments to non-residents and prepare the related returns.

faqs.q: Do you represent us in assessments?
faqs.a: We prepare reconciliations and draft explanations. Filings and representation go through your ZATCA account or a licensed representative.
